extracted.subtask_description: Front-page newspaper reports and dispatches covering wartime politics, military operations, and public affairs intended for a general readership during the 1940s war period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough study of executive branch structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough study of "the entire structure of the hydra-headed executive branch of the Federal government" by competent and impartial officials who would consult industrial, agricultural, labor and other interests which might be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct by competent, impartial officials; consult affected industrial, agricultural, labor and other interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidate non-essential agencies and eliminate 'political featherbeds'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'All agencies, boards, bureaus and commissions which are not performing an essential governmental function should be immediately liquidated,' and 'political featherbeds' should be eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate liquidation of nonessential bodies and removal of patronage/featherbed positions to streamline government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place independent agencies under responsible head and streamline divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'All essential agencies now having an independent status should be placed under the jurisdiction of a responsible head,' and various intra-department divisions should be streamlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize oversight by placing independent agencies under responsible heads and reduce intra-department fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select cabinet members based on qualifications and delegate authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabinet members or department heads should be chosen 'on the basis of their particular qualifications for the job,' and adequate authority should be delegated to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint on merit and ensure appointments are given sufficient delegated authority to perform duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial reduction in governmental job holders
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial reduction in the number of governmental job holders, with 'hundreds of thousands of them' sent back to private employment or released to the armed forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale workforce reduction in government positions, with reallocation to private sector or military service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closer working relationship between executive and legislative branches
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'closer working relationship between the executive and legislative branches of the Federal government.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve coordination and cooperation between executive and legislative branches to enhance governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Presidential tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit Presidential tenure to two four-year terms or one six-year term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impose term limits on the presidency to restrict duration in office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter censorship of alarmist phraseology in war reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime Minister Churchill asked for 'stricter censorship of alarmist phraseology' in reports of the fighting in Italy and said 'such words as "desperate" ought not to be used in a battle of this kind when they are false, and still less are they to be used if they are true.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid alarmist language that needlessly distresses the public or, if true, could encourage the enemy; base reassuring statements on commanders' statements and balance press liberty with troop safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondents' discretion and responsibility near front lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents at the front 'discharged their duties with very great discretion,' Churchill said, noting the wish and desire of correspondents to discharge responsibilities and help troops but also acknowledging that accidents will happen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-line reporters should exercise discretion, coordinate with military communications, avoid alarmist or misleading dispatches, and be mindful of the potential impact on troops and public morale.
